name: NY-25
label: Safe D

key_factors: D+10 district with incumbent Joseph Morelle seeking re-election
Overwhelming financial edge: Morelle raised $2.2M with outside support; McIntyre raised $47K with under $2K on hand
Prediction markets price a Democratic win near 97%
No public general-election polling, so the outlook rests on fundamentals
model.rationale: A district leaning Democratic by ten points, a well-funded incumbent facing a challenger with negligible resources, no outside spending against him, and markets pricing the race near 97% Democratic all point the same direction, supporting a Safe D rating with a margin in the low twenties.
model.watch: Late outside spending against Morelle or a sharp national shift toward Republicans could narrow the expected margin, though no current evidence suggests the seat is competitive.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.

overview:
Joseph Morelle, the Democratic incumbent, seeks another term in a Rochester-area district that leans Democratic by about ten points. He has raised roughly $2.2 million and holds a large cash advantage, while Republican Virginia McIntyre has raised under $50,000 and reported less than $2,000 on hand. No outside groups are spending against Morelle, and prediction markets put his chances near 97%.

No public general-election polling covers the race, so the outlook rests on district fundamentals, the incumbency advantage, and the stark resource gap. Those factors all point the same direction, suggesting a comfortable Democratic margin in the low twenties. The main sources of uncertainty are the absence of polling and the possibility of a late shift in the national environment, but nothing in the available evidence indicates the seat is in play.
